title: Implement frontend UI platform shutdown control and user notification system
description: Add a protected administrative shutdown control in the UI with multi-factor or double-confirmation modal. Display a graceful maintenance/shutdown banner and countdown timer to connected users, disable new transactional submissions, and trigger the backend graceful shutdown workflow while rendering real-time drain and shutdown status.
close_reason: Implemented frontend UI platform shutdown control with: double-confirmation modal, global shutdown banner with countdown timer, transactional form disabling, backend shutdown trigger via /admin/shutdown, real-time status polling via /actuator/shutdown-status, accessibility support, and responsive design. All tests pass.

title: Implement graceful backend shutdown and traffic draining across microservices
description: Configure Spring Boot graceful shutdown (server.shutdown=graceful, spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase) across all platform services and gateway. Enable and secure the Spring Boot Actuator /actuator/shutdown endpoint. Implement lifecycle hooks to drain active in-flight requests, flush message buffers, release database connection pools gracefully, and deregister from service discovery / gateway before process exit.
notes:
Implemented graceful shutdown + traffic draining.

New package com.spring.api.hub.lifecycle:
- GracefulShutdownCoordinator: on ContextClosedEvent, flips ReadinessState.REFUSING_TRAFFIC (drives /actuator/health/readiness to OUT_OF_SERVICE), then refuses new business requests, deregisters, ends streaming feeds/buffers, then waits for in-flight work.
- InFlightRequestTracker: counts in-flight requests, awaitQuiescence(timeout).
- DrainGateWebFilter: 503 + Retry-After while draining; management endpoints exempt in both directions (a shutdown request must not wait on itself).
- ShutdownTokenWebFilter: guards /actuator/shutdown, constant-time compare. Fails closed: no token provisioned -> 404; wrong token -> 401.
- DrainSignal + MessageBufferRegistry: end the never-ending SSE feeds and hotSink.
- ServiceDeregistration SPI + LoggingServiceDeregistration default; a discovery client just publishes another bean.

Config: server.shutdown=graceful, timeout-per-shutdown-phase=30s, actuator exposure health/info/shutdown, health probes enabled, show-details=never, platform.shutdown.drain-timeout=20s, shutdown-token from HUB_SHUTDOWN_TOKEN (blank = endpoint disabled).

Key fix: the Jenkins SSE feeds polled forever, so every shutdown would have stalled for the full drain timeout. They now use takeUntilOther(drainSignal.drain()).

Incidental fix: adding actuator made RequestMappingHandlerMapping ambiguous (gateway + actuator each contribute one). NavigationService now injects by bean name, and actuator paths are excluded from the site navigation.

Verified: 98 tests, 1 failure (HubApplicationTests.contextLoads, pre-existing: committed application.properties has literal <username>/<password> placeholders and no MySQL). Confirmed it passes with a real DB via SPRING_APPLICATION_JSON. Also verified against a running jar: SIGTERM during an open SSE stream ends it cleanly and shuts down in order. Docs in hub/SHUTDOWN.md.

title: Move DB credentials out of git into environment variables or local properties
description: Stop storing DB credentials in git. Move username/password out of src/main/resources/application.properties into env vars or a gitignored application-local.properties. The file currently has a live MySQL password.

title: Admin shutdown endpoints are unauthenticated: /admin/shutdown proxies the shutdown token for any caller
description:
## Summary
`POST /admin/shutdown` in the hub has no authentication or authorization. Any caller that can reach the hub can trigger a full platform shutdown whenever `platform.shutdown.shutdown-token` is configured.

## Why this matters
`ShutdownTokenWebFilter` protects `POST /actuator/shutdown` with the shared secret, but `AdminController.initiateShutdown()` reads that secret server-side and forwards it. The token therefore only protects the actuator from direct external calls; it does not protect the UI proxy. The admin page/controller has no Spring Security chain and is reachable by anyone who can reach the hub.

## Evidence
- `hub/src/main/java/com/spring/api/hub/controllers/AdminController.java` (`POST /admin/shutdown`, no auth checks)
- `hub/src/main/java/com/spring/api/hub/lifecycle/ShutdownTokenWebFilter.java` (token only guards the actuator path)
- No `SecurityFilterChain`/`EnableWebSecurity` exists in the repository.

## Suggested direction
Authenticate/authorize `/admin/**` (and specifically the shutdown POST) before proxying, and return 401/403 for anonymous callers. Consider CSRF protection for the state-changing POST and rate limiting/audit logging.

## Acceptance criteria
- Anonymous `POST /admin/shutdown` is rejected (401/403) and never reaches the actuator.
- Authorized admin flow still works from the admin UI.
- CSRF protection applies to the shutdown form/endpoint.
- Access attempts (allowed and denied) are audit-logged.

title: Admin/shutdown/status page not working as expected when initiating Platform Shutdown
description:
## Summary
The Admin > Platform Shutdown UI reports a successful shutdown when none was initiated, then immediately reports the platform as offline. Status polling never reflects real drain progress.

## Root causes (verified in code)
1. **Actuator endpoint not exposed** — `hub/src/main/resources/application.properties` (and `application-dev.properties`) expose `health,info,shutdown` but NOT `shutdown-status`. `GET /actuator/shutdown-status` therefore returns 404.
2. **404 is treated as "shutdown complete"** — `shutdown.js:240-243` maps a 404 from the status endpoint to `handleShutdownComplete()`, so the first poll after clicking the button paints 100% and "Platform Offline" even though nothing happened.
3. **Admin endpoint always returns HTTP 200** — `AdminController.initiateShutdown()` returns `{success:false}` with 200 when the token is missing (default `HUB_SHUTDOWN_TOKEN=` is empty). `shutdown.js:178` only checks `response.ok` and never reads `data.success`, so it logs "Shutdown initiated successfully" and starts polling anyway.
4. **Status contract mismatch** — `ShutdownStatusEndpoint` never returns `complete`; `shutdown.js:252` requires `data.draining === false && data.complete === true`, so completion is never detected from JSON. `getPhaseLabel()` also tests `data.draining` before `data.complete`, making "Shutdown Complete" unreachable.
5. **Progress ignored** — the endpoint returns `progressPercent`, but the UI recomputes progress client-side from a click-time timer (wrong if the page was loaded mid-drain or the POST failed).
6. **Dead admin status API** — `AdminController#getShutdownStatus()` hardcodes `draining:false` and omits in-flight/complete/progress, despite being documented as the UI polling endpoint.

## Expected
- Clicking "Initiate Platform Shutdown" with a token configured starts draining and the panel shows real phase, in-flight count, and progress from `/actuator/shutdown-status`.
- Missing/invalid token surfaces an error toast and does NOT mark the platform offline.
- A 404/unreachable status endpoint is reported as "status unavailable", not "shutdown complete".
- Completion is detected only when the server signals it.

## Acceptance criteria
- `shutdown-status` exposed in both prod and dev profiles; endpoint reachable while draining.
- UI does not declare success unless `success:true`.
- UI never renders "Platform Offline" on a 404/network error.
- Status endpoint returns `complete`; UI uses server `progressPercent` and `inFlightRequests`.
- Admin status endpoint delegates to `GracefulShutdownCoordinator`/`InFlightRequestTracker` instead of hardcoding values.
- Tests cover token-missing POST and 404 status handling.
notes:
Implementation started (claimed).

## Changes made
1. `application.properties`, `application-dev.properties`, `application-template.properties`: added `shutdown-status` to `management.endpoints.web.exposure.include`.
2. `GracefulShutdownCoordinator`: added `completed` state with `isDraining()`/`isComplete()`, set in a `finally` so a failed step still ends the drain state.
3. `ShutdownStatusEndpoint`: now returns `complete`, derives `draining` from the coordinator, reports `progressPercent` 0/95/100 with in-flight heuristic, removed unused `DrainSignal` dependency.
4. `AdminController`:
   - `POST /admin/shutdown` now returns 503 when no token is configured and 502 when the actuator call fails (was always 200 with success:false).
   - Actuator base path is configurable instead of hardcoded.
   - `GET /admin/shutdown/status` now returns real `draining`/`complete`/`inFlightRequests`/`progressPercent` from the coordinator and tracker.
5. `shutdown.js`:
   - Treats non-OK responses and `success:false` as failures; does not poll on failure.
   - 404 on the status endpoint is now "Status Unavailable", not "Platform Offline".
   - Detects completion only from `data.complete === true`; `getPhaseLabel()` checks completion first.
   - Uses server `progressPercent`, and reads drain timeout on page load.
6. Tests: extended `AdminControllerTest` (503 without token, real status payload) and added `ShutdownStatusEndpointTest` (4 cases).

## Confirmation dialog fix (reported by user)
- Root cause: `.modal-backdrop` was a `position: fixed; inset: 0` transparent div inside the `<dialog>`, painted above the non-positioned `.modal-content`. Every click, including on the confirmation checkboxes, hit the backdrop and ran `closeModal()`.
- Removed the overlay div from `admin.html`, removed the dead `.modal-backdrop` CSS rule, and replaced the backdrop listener with a native-backdrop check in `shutdown.js` (`e.target === dialog` only). Checkboxes now receive clicks and can only close the dialog via Cancel/X/Escape/backdrop.

## Verification
`:hub:test` passes (AdminControllerTest 7/7, ShutdownStatusEndpointTest 4/4, GracefulShutdownHttpTests 8/8). `node --check shutdown.js` OK. `grep modal-backdrop` returns no references.

## Remaining / follow-ups
- Manual browser verification of the confirmation dialog (checkbox toggling, confirm button enablement) and the full shutdown flow with/without HUB_SHUTDOWN_TOKEN.
- If `management.server.port` is ever set to a different port, `shutdown.js` still polls a relative `/actuator/shutdown-status`; the UI needs the management port injected.
- `application-dev.properties` is gitignored, so the dev-profile exposure change stays local.
- Separate issue created for the unauthenticated /admin/shutdown proxy.
close_reason: Verified by user: confirmation checkboxes work, shutdown flow works with HUB_SHUTDOWN_TOKEN. Fixes: expose shutdown-status endpoint, real complete/draining/progress contract, 503/502 on failed shutdown, UI no longer treats 404 as offline, removed overlay that blocked modal checkboxes. :hub:test green (19 tests across affected classes).

description: Define requirements, architectural impact, data model changes, API contracts, and acceptance criteria before writing code.
design:
## API Gateway Service Architecture

### Current State
- Hub (port 8082) contains GatewayConfig with disabled routing to avoid loopback conflicts with internal controllers
- Hub has ProductAutomationController and JenkinsController at /products/automation/**
- Automation-service runs on port 8081
- Api-gateway service exists at port 8080 but is minimally configured

### Target Architecture
1. **Move GatewayConfig** from hub to api-gateway service
2. **Configure Dynamic Routing**:
   - /products/automation/** → automation-service:8081
   - Remove gateway dependencies from hub
   - Hub keeps only its own business logic endpoints
3. **Rate Limiting**: Token bucket / Redis-based rate limiting per client/IP
4. **Circuit Breakers**: Resilience4j integration for downstream service protection

### Data Model
- No new data models needed for gateway
- Route configuration via application.yml / RouteLocator beans

### API Contracts
- Gateway exposes /actuator/health, /actuator/info, /actuator/metrics
- Routes /products/automation/** to automation-service
- Preserves path stripping/rewriting as needed

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] api-gateway starts on port 8080
- [ ] GatewayConfig moved from hub to api-gateway
- [ ] Dynamic routing to automation-service works
- [ ] Rate limiting configured (default: 100 req/s per IP)
- [ ] Circuit breakers configured with Resilience4j
- [ ] Hub no longer has spring-cloud-starter-gateway dependency
- [ ] Hub internal controllers at /products/automation/** removed or relocated
- [ ] Integration tests pass
acceptance_criteria: api-gateway starts on port 8080; GatewayConfig moved from hub to api-gateway; Dynamic routing /products/automation/** → automation-service:8081 works; Rate limiting configured (100 req/s per IP default); Circuit breakers configured with Resilience4j; Hub no longer has spring-cloud-starter-gateway dependency; Hub internal controllers at /products/automation/** removed; Integration tests pass

title: Offload blocking JPA operations from Netty event loop to boundedElastic scheduler
description: Keep JPA off the Netty event loop. Hub is WebFlux; AutomationRepository.save and friends are blocking. Wrap DB work in Mono.fromCallable(...).subscribeOn(Schedulers.boundedElastic()) (you already do a similar CompletableFuture pattern in JenkinsController.getJenkinsConfigMono).

title: Fix Gateway route loopback on /products/** fighting internal controllers
description: Don’t treat Gateway as a gateway yet. GatewayConfig sends /products/** back to localhost:8082. Either remove that route or point it at a real downstream service. As written it can fight your own controllers.

title: Fix /admin SQL injection vulnerability by sanitizing tableName
description: Fix /admin SQL. AdminController concatenates tableName into CREATE/SELECT/DROP. That’s easy to break and unsafe. Reuse the sanitizing idea already in AdminService, or drop this UI until you need it.

Add an equivalent Windows launcher (start-hub.ps1 preferred, or .bat) that mirrors it: start the MySQL compose service, wait for readiness, then run the hub via 'gradlew bootRun' or the packaged jar, with the same flags (profile, skip-db, detach) and env-based credentials (MYSQL_PASSWORD/MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD, HUB_SHUTDOWN_TOKEN). Reference: hub/scripts/start-hub.sh.

title: Create bash script to start the hub application
description: Need a bash script to start up the hub application. Should handle launching the required services/processes for the hub, with sensible defaults and basic error handling.
